record.paper_title: Exactly unsolved problems of interacting 1D fermions
record.context_brief: validity of the Boltzmann current formula with non-diagonal bulk flavor scattering
record.original_question: For the one-dimensional s-d exchange tunneling Hamiltonian, can the non-equilibrium current be computed by a Boltzmann/rate-equation formula that integrates the difference of the two quasiparticle occupation densities times the squared flavor-changing scattering amplitude, despite the fact that in the original lead basis flavor-changing scattering occurs throughout the bulk and the bias charge is not diagonal on Bethe-ansatz states?

evidence.quote: The non-conservation of flavor is also explicitly present in this term: the in-state |1i ⊗ |1i will be mapped to the supperposition of |1i ⊗|1i and |2i ⊗|2i. So, the scattering of particles of first kind into particles of the second kind occurs not only on the impurity, but also in the bulk.
Then, based on the probabilistic arguments, one employes the Bolzmann rate equation to obtain the current: I ∼ ∫ dǫ[n1(ǫ, µ) − n2(ǫ, µ)]|S12(ǫ)|2.
The flavor z-projection Y0 is not diagonal on the Bethe ansatz states. This leads to some technical difficulties, as well as to the question of the applicability of (42) for such situations.
Can one apply Eq (42) to the model (5)-(7)?

artifact.category_tag: 1D interacting fermions and Bethe ansatz transport
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional s–d exchange tunneling model describing two species ("flavors") of fermions in a lead coupled to a localized magnetic impurity. In the original lead basis the Hamiltonian has the schematic form

  H = H_0 + H_int + H_imp,

where H_0 is the kinetic part for two flavors of left- and right-moving fermions ψ_a(x), a=1,2, H_int contains current–current bulk interactions that, when diagonalized by a Bogoliubov/rotation transformation, mix the two flavors throughout the bulk (so that an in-state |1⟩⊗|1⟩ is mapped to a superposition of |1⟩⊗|1⟩ and |2⟩⊗|2⟩), and H_imp is a flavor-changing exchange coupling localized at x=0 to an impurity spin. A bias µ is applied that, in the original lead basis, would be implemented by a charge operator Y_0 (the flavor z-projection) which, however, is not diagonal on the exact Bethe-ansatz eigenstates of H.

Let n_a(ε,µ) (a=1,2) denote the non-equilibrium quasiparticle occupation densities of the two Bethe-ansatz flavors in the presence of the bias µ, and let S_{12}(ε) denote the on-shell flavor-changing scattering amplitude off the impurity at energy ε.

Question: Is the steady-state non-equilibrium current through the impurity given by the Boltzmann/rate-equation expression

  I(µ) = C ∫ dε [ n_1(ε,µ) − n_2(ε,µ) ] |S_{12}(ε)|^2

(with C a model-independent constant), notwithstanding the fact that in the original lead basis flavor-changing scattering takes place not only at the impurity but also throughout the bulk, and that the bias charge Y_0 is not diagonal on the Bethe-ansatz states? Equivalently, does the naive probabilistic rate-equation derivation remain valid for this Hamiltonian, and if so, under what precise conditions?
artifact.status_search_result: No specific published resolution of the validity of the Boltzmann/rate-equation current formula for this particular s–d tunneling model with non-diagonal bulk flavor scattering and non-diagonal bias charge on Bethe-ansatz states could be located. The status appears unverified in the available literature.
